summary: Cross-namespace embedding cache leak causing sporadic rerank tail latency and degraded top-k stability
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent large tail latencies (up to +6s) on rerank endpoint and observed instability in top-k results for identical queries. Impact: NimbusDocs (dedicated) saw user-facing search slowdowns in production us-east-1 starting 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC; automated rollout of a content indexing job coincided with the onset. Environment: Dedicated pool for NimbusDocs pinned to redwood-rerank-v2 with embed-ingest streaming from customer namespace 'nimbus-main'. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run their nightly ingest + rerank workload (batch size ~128) against /v1/rerank 2) Observe increased request latency and occasional missing top-1 results compared to baseline 3) Restarting the embed-proxy transiently decreases tail latency and restores top-k consistency. Logs/observations: - Metrics show cache eviction anomalies and a spike in cross-namespace cache lookups starting at 22:28 UTC. - Rerank request traces show repeated cache misses followed by CPU fallback path and queueing in the serving runtime. - Customer provided sample request IDs: req-NIM-20260309-1A, req-NIM-20260309-1B. Customer quote: "Search latency climbed and users reported wrong top results after our index job. Restart fixed it for an hour."
comments: 2026-03-10 08:14 UTC - Asha Patel (Support): Initial triage, escalated to SRE. Collected request IDs and asked for traces and sample payloads.

2026-03-10 09:03 UTC - Marco Delgado (SRE): Correlated spike with embed-ingest job from NimbusDocs. Noted unusual cache churn and an increase in cross-namespace lookup rate. Opened INT-441 for internal cache investigation.
2026-03-10 13:21 UTC - NimbusDocs (Customer): Provided additional traces and a reproduction script. Mentioned rollback to previous embed version temporarily resolved the issue.

2026-03-11 02:46 UTC - Priya Menon (Infra): Observed that embed-proxy kept stale namespace mappings after schema migration, causing some embeddings to be stored under a shared shard. Hypothesis: namespace key normalization bug introduced cross-tenant contamination in the in-memory cache.
2026-03-11 11:12 UTC - Marco Delgado (SRE): Applied temporary rule to pin NimbusDocs traffic to an isolated cache shard and added aggressive TTL on affected cache keys. Monitoring for reappearance.

2026-03-12 07:05 UTC - Asha Patel (Support): Notified customer about mitigation and asked to validate whether search behavior returned to normal. Customer reported improvement but intermittent anomalies remain during high ingest cycles.
investigation_notes: Cache telemetry shows sudden increase in 'namespace_mismatch_lookup' metric aligned with customer indexing window.
Trace samples indicate rerank flow falls back to CPU scorer when KV cache misses exceed threshold, causing +200-600ms per request and occasional queueing under burst.
Embed-proxy logs contain WARN entries: 'normalized_namespace mismatch -> fallback to default shard' for ~0.7% of embeddings during migration window.
Reproduction locally: running the customer's ingest job with synthetic collisions reproduces cache spillover and rerank tail latency within 30 minutes.

Root cause hypothesis: a schema migration changed namespace-normalization rules in embed-proxy, leaving a transient state where older ingesters wrote embeddings under legacy keys while new readers expected normalized keys. This caused cache shard affinity flips and increased cross-shard lookups.

Risk: potential for cross-tenant contamination of cache entries (not of persistent storage) and recurring latency regressions during heavy ingest/rollout windows. No evidence of customer data exfiltration in persistent stores found so far.

Mitigations tested: 1) Pinning cache shard for NimbusDocs removes cross-namespace lookups and restores normal tail latency. 2) Forcing a namespace rehash migration on a canary replica prevents re-contamination but needs coordinated rollout.
resolution: Mitigation in place: pinned NimbusDocs to a dedicated cache shard and set aggressive TTLs on suspected stale keys. Customer reports noticeable improvement; tail latency reduced to baseline during subsequent ingest windows. Next steps: schedule a coordinated embed-proxy migration rollout with a compatibility shim that accepts both legacy and normalized namespace keys for 72 hours, add automated sanity checks to detect namespace-mismatch metrics, and implement an emergency kill-switch to pin shards per-customer. Follow-up ticket INT-512 created to implement migration shim and long-term fix.
next_steps: INT-512: Implement compatibility shim in embed-proxy to read legacy and normalized keys for 72h rollout window
Add alert: namespace_mismatch_lookup > 0.1% for 15m triggers P1 alert to SRE and Support
Automate shard-pinning runbook for dedicated customers during migrations
Coordinate with NimbusDocs on a maintenance window for safe migration and validation
